preamble: Retroflexion of the lateral [l] to [ɭ]. In the western and southern Indo-Aryan languages (Marathi, Gujarati, Odia, Rajasthani, Punjabi), single intervocalic Old Indo-Aryan -l- became retroflex -ḷ- [ɭ], while geminate -ll- stayed dental, so Sanskrit phala 'fruit' gives Marathi and Gujarati phaḷ and Odia phaḷa. Independently, in Eastern and Trøndelag Norwegian the sequence /rl/ coalesces into a retroflex lateral [ɭ].

examples.note: Intervocalic single -l- of Old Indo-Aryan surfaces as the retroflex lateral ळ.
The learned doublet ફલ phal keeps dental [l].
Coalescence: the tap and the lateral fuse into a single retroflex lateral; spreading of retroflex [ɭ] to other contexts is ongoing in Oslo speech.

sources: Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
Kristoffersen, G. (2000). The Phonology of Norwegian. Oxford University Press.
